disclaimer: Figures were checked on the as_of date from the sources listed and go stale quickly. Verify with WHO, Africa CDC and the national Ministry of Health before any decision.

threats.status: Active. Public health emergency of international concern reported on 16 May 2026.
threats.figures: DRC: 9,552 confirmed cases and 4,602 deaths (to 19 Oct). Kenya: 8 confirmed cases and 1 death (to 20 Oct); the first case was imported and reported on 6 Oct.
threats.note: Uganda declared its outbreak over on 27 Aug 2026 after a 42 day countdown. Specific vaccines and treatments were still under investigation in October 2026.

profile.spread: Contact with blood or body fluids of a sick person or a body. Funerals and health care settings carry high risk.

threats.status: No active outbreak found. Ethiopia's first outbreak was declared over on 26 Jan 2026.
threats.figures: Ethiopia: 14 confirmed cases and 9 deaths, 857 contacts followed (Nov 2025 to Jan 2026).
threats.note: Spillover from animal reservoirs such as fruit bats can cause new outbreaks. Marburg outbreaks have occurred in Tanzania in the last five years. No licensed vaccine or treatment.

profile.spread: Close contact with body fluids of an infected person or contaminated surfaces. Fruit bats are the animal source.

sources.title: AP via WTOP: Ethiopia declares end of Marburg outbreak
Healio: Ethiopia's first Marburg outbreak is over

threats.status: Ongoing at lower intensity. Africa CDC lifted its continental emergency in January 2026.
threats.figures: WHO report of 14 Sept 2026: 11 African countries had active transmission between 6 Jul and 16 Aug 2026, with 1,153 confirmed cases and 7 deaths. 35 African countries affected since Jan 2025.
threats.note: The country list is in the WHO report. Add the affected countries to this entry so Sentinel can calculate exposure.

profile.spread: Close contact with a person with lesions, including household and sexual contact. Vaccination is part of the response.

threats.status: El Niño advisory, strengthening (NOAA update of 10 Sept 2026).
threats.figures: NOAA: greater than 90% chance of a very strong event in the 2026 to 2027 northern winter, and a 75% chance of a historic event in October to December 2026.
threats.note: The 8 October update was not checked. Check ICPAC for the East Africa seasonal forecast.
